hypotheses.statement: These formulas define infinite-dimensional Banach spaces after completion. Coordinate evaluations and the fields extend continuously. If $H$ is a finite set containing the root and all predecessors of its nodes, then coordinate restriction $\Pi_H$ is a contractive projection. Its kernel $F_H$ has finite codimension, and finitely supported elements of $F_H$ are dense in $F_H$. Both $X_0$ and $X_J$ are reflexive.

Let $J$ be a subset of the leaves of a finite tree with root $o$. Suppose that $P,Q,P',Q'$ are nonnegative fields, each satisfying $$A_s^2\ge\sum_{c\in\operatorname{ch}(s)}A_c^2$$ at every internal node, for each $A\in\{P,Q,P',Q'\}$. Suppose also that $P'-P=Q'-Q=d\ge0$, and that at each internal node at least one of the inequalities for $P,Q$ is an equality. If $P_b=Q_b=0$ for $b\in J$, then $$\sum_{b\in J}d_b^2
 \le\bigl[d_o(2P_o+d_o)(2Q_o+d_o)\bigr]^{2/3}.$$

Let $N=N_\Sigma$ or $N=N_J$. Suppose that $x$ is a finitely supported unit vector and that $z\in F_H$, where $H$ is a finite initial set containing $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}x$. If $$d=\frac12\left(\frac{N(x+z)+N(x-z)}2-1\right),$$ then $d\ge0$ and $N(z)^3\le64d(1+d)^2$.

Let $X$ be a Banach space. Suppose that for every $h\ge1$ there are vectors $u_s^{(h)}$, indexed by $s\in\mathbb N^{\le h}$, such that $0<m\le\|u_s^{(h)}\|\le M<\infty$ uniformly. Suppose also that for $|s|<h$ the increments $d_{s,k}^{(h)}=u_{s^\frown k}^{(h)}-u_s^{(h)}$ are weakly null as $k\to\infty$ and have norms at least $c>0$, uniformly in $h,s,k$. If $N$ is a norm and $0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty$ satisfy $\alpha\|\cdot\|\le N\le\beta\|\cdot\|$, then $$\overline\delta_N\left(\frac{\alpha c}{2\beta M}\right)=0.$$ The conclusion also holds if one infinite tree has these properties.

For each $n$, let $x_n,z_n$ be finitely supported real vectors on $\mathbb N^{<\omega}$, with $N_\Sigma(x_n)=1$. Let $H_n$ be the predecessor closure of $\operatorname{supp}x_n$, and suppose that $(z_n)_s=0$ for every $s\in H_n$. Then $$\frac{N_\Sigma(x_n+z_n)+N_\Sigma(x_n-z_n)}2\longrightarrow1
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad N_\Sigma(z_n)\longrightarrow0.$$ In particular, the assertion is uniform in the height and size of $H_n$.
For every $t>0$, the averaged asymptotic modulus of $N_\Sigma$ is positive.

Fix $M\ge\beta>0$. Let $p,q,r$ be nonnegative fields on a finite rooted tree with root $o$. Suppose that $p,q,p+r,q+r$ are upper fields, and at every nonleaf the upper inequality for at least one of $p,q$ is an equality. If $$p_o+q_o+2r_o\le M,\qquad \sum_{b\text{ a leaf}}r_b^2\ge\beta^2,$$ then $r_o\ge\gamma(M,\beta)>0$, independently of the tree. One possible choice is $$\label{log:gamma}
 \begin{gathered}
 h=\frac{\beta^2}{2M^2},\qquad c_* =\frac{\beta\sqrt h}{8},\qquad
 H_*=1+\log(M/c_*),\qquad
 K=\frac{4(2+\sqrt6)H_*}{h},\\
 \gamma(M,\beta)=\frac{\beta h}{8}e^{-K}.
 \end{gathered}$$

Let $x,y$ be finitely supported vectors in $X_J$. Suppose that $x$ is supported in a finite predecessor-closed set $H$ containing the joining root, and that $y$ vanishes on $H$. If $$N_J(x+y),N_J(x-y)\le2,
 \qquad N_J(y)\ge\zeta,\qquad 0<\zeta\le2,$$ then $$\frac{N_J(x+y)+N_J(x-y)}2
 \ge N_J(x)+2\gamma(2,\zeta/4).$$

The recursion [var:recursion] defines a norm equivalent to the usual $\ell_{p_h}(T_h)$ norm. In particular, $E_h$ is complete and reflexive, with separable dual. The space $X_{\mathrm v}$ is complete and reflexive, its dual is separable, and vectors with finite total coordinate support are dense in it. Every finite coordinate projection is bounded and has finite rank.

The space $X_{\mathrm v}$ admits no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm. More precisely, if $a\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm v}\le N\le b\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm v}$ with $0<a\le b$, then $\overline\delta_N(a/b)=0$.

Let $x,y\in E_h$, with $x$ supported on a finite ancestral set $A$ and $y$ zero on $A$. Put $B=
u_h(x)$, $Y=
u_h(y)$, and $M_\sigma=
u_h(x+\sigma y)$. With $\mathrm e=\exp(1)$ and $$c_6=2\exp(-(\mathrm e-1))4^{-6},\qquad
 U^2=M_+^2+M_-^2,$$ one has $$\label{var:sixth-component-eq}
 U^2-2B^2\ge c_6 U^{-4}Y^6.$$ A quotient with numerator and denominator both zero is interpreted as zero. The same estimate holds when $x=0$ and $y$ is arbitrary.

Let $x\in X_{\mathrm v}$ have finite total support. In each component where $x^{(h)}\ne0$, choose a finite ancestral set $A_h$ containing that support. Suppose $y\in X_{\mathrm v}$ vanishes on every such $A_h$. With $S=\|x+y\|_{\mathrm v}^2+\|x-y\|_{\mathrm v}^2$, one has $$\label{var:sixth-sum}
 S-2\|x\|_{\mathrm v}^2
 \ge c_6 S^{-2}\|y\|_{\mathrm v}^6,
 \qquad c_6=2\exp(-(\mathrm e-1))4^{-6}.$$ The right side is zero when $S=0$.

Let $x\in X_{\mathrm v}$ have finite total support. In every component with $x^{(h)}\ne0$, choose a finite ancestral set $A_h$ containing its support, and let $y\in X_{\mathrm v}$ vanish on these sets. If $R>0$ and $\|x+y\|_{\mathrm v},\|x-y\|_{\mathrm v}\le R$, then $$\label{var:cubic-sum}
 R^2\ge\|x\|_{\mathrm v}^2+
       \frac{c_3}{2\sqrt2\,R}\|y\|_{\mathrm v}^3,
 \qquad c_3=(6\mathrm e)^{-3}.$$

purpose: Midpoint convexity from two recursive potentials

coverage.checked_domain: Exhaustive integral-tight inputs: 1413 distinct trees; stars with 0..3 leaves and coordinates -2..2, chains with 2..4 nodes and coordinates -2..2, and the listed 5-node star, 5-node fork and 7-node binary tree with coordinates -1..1. All retained child squared sums admit integer roots. Boundary vectors include zero, signed singleton, zero root, opposite signs, branching and depth.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent exact enumeration of all nonnegative integer pairs satisfying the coordinate difference and squared child lower bounds, with at least one tight bound. Tightness excludes a smaller feasible real pair; no solver witness is trusted.

coverage.checked_domain: Root sum on the same finite integral-tight inputs; no common-root implementation or completed-space conclusion is certified.
coverage.oracle_basis: The root-sum output is rechecked as the sum of the independently enumerated root pair.

title: Midpoint convexity from two recursive potentials
